headline.title: Meta reportedly moves to unwind $2B Manus deal after Beijing’s demand
headline.summary: Meta is reportedly beginning to unwind its $2 billion acquisition of Manus following a directive from Beijing to reverse the deal. The move comes amid ongoing regulatory scrutiny and geopolitical tensions.

articles.title: As Anthropic suspends access to new models, India debates its AI future
articles.summary: Anthropic has suspended access to its new AI models, prompting discussions among Indian tech leaders about the implications for the country's AI development strategy. The incident is seen as a potential wake-up call for India to reassess its approach to artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Amazon security research reportedly led to the White House’s Anthropic Fable ban
articles.summary: Amazon's cybersecurity research and discussions between CEO Andy Jassy and the White House reportedly influenced the decision to impose export controls on Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5. This directive, as reported by the Wall Street Journal, was part of broader security concerns.

articles.title: Anthropic cuts off Fable 5 and Mythos 5 access following government order
articles.summary: Anthropic has complied with a government order to block access to its AI models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, for all foreign nations, including its own employees, due to national security concerns. As a result, the company has completely restricted access to these models for all customers.

articles.title: SFT Drives Gemini’s Safety Properties
articles.summary: Google DeepMind's Language Model Interpretability team has released a research update indicating that the safety properties of the Gemini model are primarily influenced by the combination of pretraining and supervised fine-tuning (SFT), rather than reinforcement learning. The findings suggest that these safety characteristics may not apply universally to other model families.

articles.title: KPMG pulls report on AI usage due to apparent hallucinations
articles.summary: KPMG has retracted a report on AI usage after discovering inaccuracies attributed to the technology's tendency to produce hallucinations. This incident highlights ongoing concerns regarding the reliability of AI-generated information.

articles.title: My yard is dying, so I made an app for that
articles.summary: A developer created an app to address issues in their yard, utilizing AI technology to generate a functional prototype quickly. The process included encountering a bug, which was resolved through an integrated fix option within the app.

articles.title: Amazon CEO reportedly raised Anthropic model concerns before government crackdown
articles.summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy reportedly raised security concerns regarding Anthropic's models, prompting the company to restrict global access to two of its AI models. This action comes amid increasing scrutiny and potential government regulation of AI technologies.

articles.title: Apple’s new AI photo editing tools mostly work, for better and worse
articles.summary: Apple has introduced new AI photo editing tools in iOS 27, marking a significant update for its camera capabilities. While these features show promise, they are considered less advanced compared to those available on competitors like Google's Pixel phones.

articles.title: The future of Hollywood isn’t feeding prompts into vanilla gen AI models
articles.summary: Despite the buzz surrounding generative AI's potential in filmmaking, no significant projects have emerged that resonate with audiences as viable entertainment options. Current AI video models primarily produce short clips rather than full-length features that could attract viewers.

articles.title: OpenAI faces investigation from state attorneys general
articles.summary: OpenAI is under investigation by state attorneys general regarding various practices, including its advertising policies and the management of health data. The specific states involved in the inquiry have not been disclosed.

articles.title: Anthropic Says It’s Taking Claude Fable 5 Offline to Comply With US Government Order
articles.summary: Anthropic announced it is taking its Claude Fable 5 AI model offline to comply with a US government order due to concerns about potential methods for bypassing its safeguards. The company stated that the decision was made in response to the government's awareness of a possible "jailbreaking" technique.
